titleEn: Constantly on edge at work? It could be anticipatory stress
titleZh: 工作时总是紧绷？可能是预期性压力
method: Machine reference translation with paragraph alignment; not manually certified.

paragraphs.en: In Nosferatu (1922), one of cinema’s most haunting images arrives before the vampire himself: his shadow. Something is approaching, but we don’t know exactly what it is, or what will happen when it arrives. The fear lies in the anticipation.
paragraphs.zh: 在《诺斯费拉图》（1922）中，电影中最令人难以忘怀的画面之一出现在吸血鬼本人面前：他的影子。有什么东西正在接近，但我们不知道它到底是什么，也不知道它到来时会发生什么。恐惧在于预期。

paragraphs.en: This is called anticipatory stress, and it can affect us in our work lives. An event may be months away, yet psychologically it has already entered the room, casting a shadow on the present.
paragraphs.zh: 这就是所谓的预期压力，它会影响我们的工作生活。一件事可能是几个月后的事，但在心理上它已经进入房间，给现在投下阴影。

paragraphs.en: In my research, I explored the wellbeing at work of university education academics working within high-stakes inspection and accountability systems in the UK and Ireland.
paragraphs.zh: 在我的研究中，我探讨了在英国和爱尔兰的高风险检查和问责制系统内工作的大学教育学者的工作福祉。

paragraphs.en: In England, all initial teacher education providers are inspected by Ofsted. In other nations, accreditation inspections may be conducted by professional regulatory bodies, such as the Teaching Council of Ireland. Across these different systems, many academics described feeling anticipatory stress while waiting for an inspection.
paragraphs.zh: 在英格兰，所有的初始教师教育机构都由Ofsted进行检查。在其他国家，认证检查可能由专业监管机构进行，例如爱尔兰的教学理事会。在这些不同的系统中，许多学者描述了等待检查时的预期压力。

paragraphs.en: Participants in England described living in “constant anticipation”, on “constant red alert” and “on a knife edge” while waiting for the call from Ofsted.
paragraphs.zh: 英格兰的参与者描述了在等待Ofsted电话时“不断期待”，“不断红色警报”和“刀锋”的生活。

paragraphs.en: The inspection had not begun, but the expectation of it was already shaping how they worked, where they directed their attention and even how confidently they could make plans outside work. As one participant said, “every family plan is prefaced with, ‘but I could get the call’”.
paragraphs.zh: 检查还没有开始，但对它的期望已经影响了他们的工作方式，他们将注意力集中在哪里，甚至他们在工作之外制定计划的信心有多大。正如一位参与者所说，“每个家庭计划的开头都是，'但我可以接到电话'”。

paragraphs.en: Anticipation itself is not the problem. It’s a normal psychological function that allows us to prepare for what is coming. The difficulty arises when we know something important is approaching, but our personal control is limited, and we don’t have enough information to decide what useful preparation actually looks like.
paragraphs.zh: 预期本身并不是问题所在。它是一种正常的心理功能，让我们为即将到来的事情做好准备。当我们知道重要的事情即将到来时，困难就出现了，但我们的个人控制能力有限，我们没有足够的信息来决定实际上有用的准备是什么样子。

paragraphs.en: Under those conditions, the mind keeps working on the problem. We forecast possible outcomes, we revisit conversations we have had and we can become more attentive to potential signals.
paragraphs.zh: 在这种情况下，我们的大脑会继续思考这个问题，我们会预测可能的结果，我们会重新审视我们已经进行过的对话，我们会更加关注潜在的信号。

paragraphs.en: An unexpected request for a meeting or a delayed email response can suddenly acquire particular significance, not necessarily because it means anything, but because uncertainty can make us more vigilant for information that might help predict what comes next.
paragraphs.zh: 一个意外的会议请求或延迟的电子邮件回复可能会突然变得特别重要，不一定是因为它意味着什么，而是因为不确定性可以让我们对可能有助于预测接下来会发生什么的信息更加警惕。

paragraphs.en: Psychologists use the term “perseverative cognition” to describe how worry and rumination can keep a potential stressor mentally active when it is not actually present. In simple terms, the stressful event may be absent, but the mind keeps bringing it back into the present.
paragraphs.zh: 心理学家用“持续性认知”来描述焦虑和沉思是如何在潜在的压力源不存在的情况下保持精神活跃的。简单地说，压力事件可能不存在，但大脑会不断地把它带回到现在。

paragraphs.en: As one of my interviewees explained: “My mind has already gone into overdrive with worry – even though the inspection might not take place until next year.” Another said: “It’s the ‘not knowing’ that I find so stressful.” Indeed, research into uncertain threat suggests that unpredictability can sustain vigilance, partly because there is no clear point at which we know we can safely stand down.
paragraphs.zh: 正如我的一位受访者所解释的那样：“我的脑子里已经充满了担忧--尽管检查可能要到明年才能进行。”另一位受访者说：“我感到压力很大的是'不知道'。”实际上，对不确定威胁的研究表明，不可预测性可以维持警惕，部分原因是我们没有一个明确的点，可以让我们知道自己可以安全地退出。

paragraphs.en: Stressful events at work
paragraphs.zh: 工作中的压力事件

paragraphs.en: Many of the events we anticipate at work also carry an element of evaluation. An inspection, promotion process or performance review can place our competence directly under scrutiny, while restructuring may raise a broader question about our future value within an organisation.
paragraphs.zh: 我们在工作中预期的许多事件也带有评估的元素。检查、晋升过程或绩效评估可以直接将我们的能力置于审查之下，而重组可能会对我们在组织中的未来价值提出更广泛的问题。

paragraphs.en: Research on social-evaluative threat – the stress we feel when we think we are being judged by others – suggests that these situations can provoke particularly strong stress responses. This was apparent in my own research. “It’s my name up front,” one participant said. “I have led the team so I feel a deep sense of personal responsibility that this goes well for everyone.”
paragraphs.zh: 对社会评价威胁--当我们认为自己受到他人评判时所感受到的压力--的研究表明，这些情况会引发特别强烈的压力反应。这在我自己的研究中就很明显。“我的名字在前面，”一名参与者说。“我领导过团队，所以我有一种深深的个人责任感，这对每个人都有利。”

paragraphs.en: Anticipation is often not only tethered to uncertainty, but to professional identity and the consequences of feeling judged.
paragraphs.zh: 预期往往不仅与不确定性有关，而且与职业认同和被评判的感觉的后果有关。

paragraphs.en: My research also showed how the period of anticipation can generate additional work. Many participants noted the gap between official advice and the reality of preparing for a high-stakes event, such as an inspection. Professional bodies might say: “Don’t do anything special for us coming,” but participants felt that, in practice, preparation was unavoidable.
paragraphs.zh: 我的研究还表明，期待期可能会产生额外的工作。许多参与者注意到，官方建议与为高风险活动（如视察）做准备的现实之间存在差距。专业机构可能会说：“不要为我们的到来做任何特别的事情”，但参与者认为，实际上，准备是不可避免的。

paragraphs.en: Some described how preparation “almost doubles your workload because you are doing your job and making sure you can demonstrate you are doing the job as well – which is very stressful”. This may be familiar to those in other work contexts. Employees often have to deliver their work while documenting, checking and preparing to account for it. When this preparation takes place in the light of a high-stakes event, it can easily be accompanied by anticipatory stress.
paragraphs.zh: 一些人描述说，准备工作“几乎使你的工作量加倍，因为你在做你的工作，并确保你能证明你也在做这份工作--这是非常有压力的”。这可能对其他工作环境中的人来说很熟悉。员工通常必须在记录、检查和准备工作的同时交付工作。当这种准备工作发生在高风险事件中时，它很容易伴随着预期的压力。

paragraphs.en: This kind of uncertainty is becoming a familiar feature of organisational life. Restructures are announced before new roles are settled; mergers begin to reshape teams while reporting lines remain unclear.
paragraphs.zh: 这种不确定性正成为组织生活中一个熟悉的特征。在新角色确定之前，重组就已宣布;合并开始重塑团队，而报告关系仍不明确。

paragraphs.en: More recently, new technologies, such as AI, have been introduced while employees are still trying to understand what they will mean for their day-to-day work.
paragraphs.zh: 最近，人工智能等新技术已经被引入，而员工仍在试图理解这些技术对他们的日常工作意味着什么。

paragraphs.en: The difficulty isn’t change itself, nor the assumption that the change will necessarily end badly. It is the long period in which people know enough to realise that something important is shifting, but don’t have enough information to make informed decisions or understand their future with any degree of confidence.
paragraphs.zh: 困难不在于变革本身，也不假设变革必然会以糟糕的结局收场，而是人们在很长一段时间里知道足够多的信息，意识到一些重要的事情正在发生变化，但却没有足够的信息来做出明智的决定，或对自己的未来充满信心。

paragraphs.en: Organisations cannot remove all uncertainty from the workplace, and leaders cannot provide answers they do not yet have. They can, however, give uncertainty some boundaries by being clear about what is known, what aspects remain unresolved and when people can expect to know more. Without those boundaries, the period before an important event can fill with worry, rumination and attempts to make sense of incomplete information.
paragraphs.zh: 组织无法消除工作场所的所有不确定性，领导者也无法提供他们还不知道的答案。然而，他们可以通过明确哪些是已知的，哪些方面尚未解决，以及人们何时可以期望了解更多信息，来给不确定性划定一些界限。如果没有这些界限，重要事件发生前的一段时间可能充满担忧、沉思，并试图理解不完整的信息。
